M-CODE-GRAPH.NAME: Octocode code-graph adapter
M-CODE-GRAPH.purpose: Read real file-level import edges and per-file symbols from a running Octocode MCP server in a short-lived, read-only session (ADR-9), so impact/trace can be enriched without making the core gates depend on it.

export-READ_ONLY_TOOLS.PURPOSE: ADR-9 allowlist of MCP tools this adapter may call: graphrag, structural_search (view_signatures is not used — real Octocode returns full file text, not signatures).

export-collectImportEdges.PURPOSE: One MCP session; graphrag get-relationships (format:json) per supplied file; deduped, sorted imports edges; missing/broken tools → available:false + notes.

export-collectFileSymbols.PURPOSE: One graphrag search (format:json) call per file; per-file deduped symbol names/kinds from source_file inventories and symbol nodes; requested files always present.

export-parseGraphRelationships.PURPOSE: Defensive parser for recorded payloads: plain file endpoints only, imports only, dedupe/sort; invalid JSON → INTEGRATION_INVALID_OUTPUT note.

export-parseViewSignatures.PURPOSE: Defensive parser for graphrag search nodes; source_file symbol inventories + symbol kinds; dedupe per file.

CrossLink.relation: resolution, kill switch, pinned range and scrubbed child env come from ADR-9 registry
impact --code-graph maps edges to module DEPENDS and emits CODE_EDGE_UNDECLARED / DECLARED_EDGE_UNUSED
trace --code compares MODULE_MAP names with real symbols (CONTRACT_SYMBOL_MISSING)

contract.purpose: Answer two read-only questions about real code: which module files import which, and which symbols a file exports.

param.name: root
param.description: Project root; also the MCP server --path and worker cwd.

param.name: config
param.description: Supplies integrations.octocode bin/timeout and the tested range.

param.name: files
param.description: Module source files (project-relative or absolute inside root); paths outside the root are rejected.

param.name: graph
param.description: { available, version, edges[], notes[] } — notes carry INTEGRATION_* degradation codes.

error.description: Tool missing/disabled/unsupported or MCP session failed — available:false, command continues with its deterministic output.
Session or per-call timeout — note only; never a crash.
Malformed JSON or unexpected tool payload — note only; never executed as code.

notes.note-1: Read-only MCP tools only; no semantic index, no LLM calls. Octocode does initialize its local FastEmbed embedding model before answering MCP `initialize`, so the first run may download model files (see note-3).
notes.note-2: Session lifecycle: spawn octocode mcp --path <root>, initialize, optional tools/list sanity check, calls, close in finally; one session per command invocation. Startup timeout is config.integrations.octocode.timeoutMs; pre-warm models once for predictable latency.
notes.note-3: v1.7.1 root cause fixed: the pinned 0.29.2 binary starts FastEmbed before answering `initialize`; the default Jina code model is 612 MB and downloads before the handshake, which looked like a hang. With a pre-warmed cache (or smaller FastEmbed models) the session starts in ~2 s and `impact --code-graph` / `trace --code` were verified against the real binary (see analysis/octocode-startup.md).
notes.note-4: External output is untrusted data: parsed defensively, capped (4 MB/tool, 12 notes), never shell-interpolated.
